sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 3.1.9. — Let a_R = m²_R + pR. There is a canonical commutative diagram [M̃₁ ⊗_{Ŵ(R)} Ŵ(R/a_R) → φ*(M_{R/a_R}); D̃₁ ⊗_W Ŵ(R/a_R) → φ*(D) ⊗_W Ŵ(R/a_R)] where the horizontal maps are induced by the natural inclusions M̃₁ → φ*(M_R) and D̃₁ → φ*(D). Proof. — L ⊕ T be a normal decomposition for (M_{R/a_R}, M_{R/a_R,1}), and let L₀ ⊕ T₀ be the induced normal decomposition for (D, D₁).
sourceIssues.correction: The construction has to be replaced by the one of KPZ26 Lemma 5.1.15, which follows [Ho23] and, in essence, Zink's [Zi99, Theorem 3].
sourceIssues.reason: The printed recipe depends on the normal decomposition, even though its diagram commutes. An independent rank-two test: take p>2, R=Z_p[[t]], S=Ŵ(R), M=S², and the universal line generated by e₁+t e₂ modulo I_R. Two normal lifts are l=e₁+[t]e₂ and l′=l+V([t])e₂, both with T=S e₂. In M̃₁ use u=φ(l), v=p e₂. Since φ(V([t]))=p[t], the second lift gives u′=u+[t]v. After base change to B=R/(p,t²), u,v remain a free basis and [t]≠0, so the two inverse comparison maps send the same first basis vector of D̃₁ to different elements. The horizontal map loses their difference because p[t]=0 in Ŵ(B). Thus it cannot determine c. KPZ26 Lemma 5.1.15 supplies a different, functorial map; Remark 5.1.17 explains the resulting failure of Lemma 3.1.12 with the old definition of constant modulo a_R.

sourceIssues.correction: For the corrected construction, impose horizontality of the defining tensors under the canonical comparison c, equivalently the very-good condition of KPZ26 Definition 5.2.5. Then smoothness lifts the resulting tensor-preserving point and the original proofs of Lemma 3.2.14 and Propositions 3.2.17 and 3.3.13 apply. Smoothness alone does not establish horizontality. This is a missing proof/hypothesis, not an exhibited counterexample to every good embedding being very good.
sourceIssues.reason: In published KP18 §3.2.12, the prescribed reduction of Ψ must already be a point of the tensor-isomorphism torsor before smoothness can lift it. Once E1 is repaired, this requires c(sα,0)=s̃α; it is exactly the horizontality condition in published KPZ26 §5.2.1 and Definition 5.2.5. Smoothness supplies lifting of an existing torsor point, not membership of an arbitrary prescribed linear map in that torsor. Published KPZ26 §1.2.1 expressly leaves general horizontality unproved and conjectures that any good integral Hodge embedding is very good.

sourceIssues.printed: q_loc : M̃^loc_G → M^loc_{G,X} by taking (f,F) to f⁻¹(F). One sees easily that q_loc is a G-torsor. Thus we have a diagram (4.2.9) M̃^loc_G → M^loc_G, M̃^loc_G → M^loc_{G,X}, with π_loc and q_loc are G-torsors.
sourceIssues.correction: For the natural G-action in the displayed diagram, q_loc is equivariant, not in general an invariant torsor projection. Identify it instead with the action morphism G×M^loc_{G,X}→M^loc_{G,X}. It is smooth of relative dimension dim G: compose the isomorphism (g,m)↦(g,g·m) with projection. This is what the proof uses. An alternative transported G-action can make the underlying projection a torsor; that is not the action asserted in the original diagram.
sourceIssues.reason: For the natural change-of-trivialization action, q_loc transforms the image filtration, so its fibers are not G-stable when the target action is nontrivial. Hence it is not a torsor for that action. Independently, (g,m)↦(g,g·m) has inverse (g,n)↦(g,g⁻¹·n), so smoothness follows from the product projection because G is smooth. The theorem only needs equivariance and smoothness, not that both arrows be torsor projections.

sourceIssues.printed: Hence, it suffices to give a complete separated topology τ on Ŵ(A) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p such that for any x ∈ W(m_A), p^{−m}φ^m(x) → 0. Indeed, then the sum s̃ = s + Σ_{m≥0} Φ^{m+1} ∘ s ∘ Φ₀^{−m−1} − Φ^m ∘ s ∘ Φ₀^{−m} converges to an element of Hom_W(D,M) ⊗ Q_p in τ and is Frobenius invariant.
sourceIssues.correction: The ring cW(A)[1/p] is not complete for the topology τ defined there, so establishing p^{−m}φ^m(x) → 0 in τ does not finish the proof. KPZ26 show instead that cW(A)[1/p] is p-adically complete and separated and that p^{−m}φ^m(x) → 0 in the p-adic topology for x ∈ cW(M_A), which does finish it, using Zink's logarithmic coordinates on cW(pN) and [Zi01, Prop. 2.3, 2.4]. Here p-adic topology on the rationalized ring means the topology induced by its integral Ŵ(A) lattice, not the ideal-adic topology for the unit p.
sourceIssues.reason: The topology τ is induced by the product of the p-adic ghost-coordinate topologies; it permits coordinatewise limits with unbounded denominators. Explicitly take A=Z_p[ε]/(ε²), p>2, so m_A²⊂pA. In the square-zero ideal εQ_p, the Witt ghost formula is w_i(x)=p^i x_i. Let z_N have Witt coordinates ε/p^i for i≤N and zero thereafter; p^N z_N has integral finite-support coordinates, so z_N∈Ŵ(A)[1/p]. Its ghost coordinates are ε for i≤N and zero afterwards, hence (z_N) is τ-Cauchy. A limit would have all ghost coordinates ε. Multiplying by any fixed p^M would force Witt coordinates p^(M−i)ε for every i, which are not integral for i>M. Thus no limit exists even in W(A)[1/p]. KPZ26 replaces this topology by the lattice p-adic topology and proves the required decay using logarithmic coordinates.

review.reason: Checked the whole KP18 p.169 topology argument and the correction proof on KPZ26 published p.86 / v3 p.90. Added an explicit square-zero-ring Cauchy sequence witnessing incompleteness. The replacement uses the p-adic topology induced by the integral Ŵ(A) lattice, not the trivial ideal topology of p in a ring where p is invertible. In logarithmic coordinates, p^(−m)φ^m is the tail shift; tails of a p-adically null sequence tend uniformly to zero. Zink's general completeness/logarithm theorems are used as cited by KPZ26, not reproved here.

sourceIssues.printed: 4.6.21. — Let (H,Y) be a Shimura datum with H^ad a classical group. Recall ([20], cf. [43] 3.4.13) that there is central isogeny H̃ → H♯ (which depends also on Y if H has a factor of type D) such that (H,Y) is of abelian type if and only if H^der is a quotient of H♯.
sourceIssues.correction: Restrict the H♯ construction to the conditions in published KPZ26 §7.2.1 (pp.76–77): in each type-D simple factor over its totally real field, all noncompact real places must have the same Hermitian type, always D^R or always D^H. The adjoint Shimura datum being of abelian type supplies these conditions. Do not assert the construction for arbitrary classical adjoint data.
sourceIssues.reason: The required quotient is the simply connected cover at a D^R place, but the standard orthogonal quotient at a D^H place. A single central quotient cannot have a trivial kernel after one real base change and a nontrivial kernel after another: a finite central kernel in characteristic zero has constant degree. Thus the real-place compatibility condition is essential to this construction. Published KPZ26 §7.2.1 gives the precise condition and footnote 8 explicitly corrects KP18 §4.6.21. The abelian-type context used immediately afterwards satisfies the extra condition.

review.reason: Confirmed directly in the image of published KP18 p.162 and in the matching §2.3.15 passages of arXiv v3 and Kisin's author PDF. The symplectic Hodge filtration has rank g′ when dim V′=2g′; the ambient GL Grassmannian is Gr(g′,2g′), not a full-rank Grassmannian. A full-rank locally direct-summand subbundle is the whole bundle. In the rank-two case the intended generic fiber is P¹ rather than a point. No correction to this typo was found in the searched sources. Retain misprint/nothing/new.
